leaderboard.heading: Leaderboard
leaderboard.introScore: Who predicts best? For each study, participants predict the average rating that participants give it, and the prediction is scored against a target. A prediction scores 100 points, minus {penalty} for every point it is away from the target (rounded to a whole number and never below 0).
leaderboard.introTarget: The target combines the expert rating, counted as if {weight} participants had given it, with the ratings that other participants had given the study by then, in every room.
leaderboard.introRules: A participant's average score is the mean of their prediction scores over the studies they have rated, rounded to a whole percentage. Only participants who have rated at least {count} studies are ranked; anyone who has rated fewer is left out of the table. At the same average score, the participant who rated more studies is placed higher, and if that is also the same, they share a place. The table lists participants whose scores have been saved, so it can hold fewer people than the figures above. Select a nickname to see that participant's results.
leaderboard.dayNote: Showing ranked participants whose score was last updated in the past 24 hours. Their average score covers every study they have rated.
leaderboard.roomNote: Places are among participants in room {room}.
leaderboard.emptyAll: No one is ranked yet. Participants appear here once they have rated {count} studies.
leaderboard.emptyDay: No ranked participant has a score updated in the past 24 hours.

unranked.one: {count} more participant has rated fewer than {min} studies and is not ranked yet.
unranked.other: {count} more participants have rated fewer than {min} studies and are not ranked yet.

leaderboard.truncated: Only the top {count} places are listed.

criteria.heading: Which criteria matter most
criteria.intro: At the end of the workshop, each participant shares out {budget} tokens among the {count} criteria, giving more to those they think matter most when judging a study. Each bar shows the average share of tokens a criterion received. The dark line across it is the 95% confidence interval for that average (t distribution); interval limits below 0% or above 100% are shown as 0% and 100%.

count.one: Based on {count} participant who shared out all their tokens.
count.other: Based on {count} participants who shared out all their tokens.

criteria.empty: No one has shared out their tokens yet.
criteria.ciMissing: An interval needs at least two participants.

chart.heading: Ratings by study
chart.introBars: Each bar is the average quality rating that participants gave a study, on the scale from 1 to 7. Only participants' ratings count: the expert's rating is not part of the bar.
chart.introIntervals: The dark line on each bar is the 95% confidence interval for that average, worked out with the t distribution. It is long when people disagree or when few have rated the study, and missing when fewer than two have. Where an interval runs past 1 or 7, it stops at the edge of the chart without an end cap; the tooltip, the table and the study details give its full limits.
chart.introExpert: The white diamond is the expert's rating. The bar colour shows the expert's quality band, as in the key below.
chart.introTarget: The game scores predictions against a different value, the target: the expert rating counted as if {weight} participants had given it, combined with the ratings of other participants from every room. While fewer than {weight} participants have rated a study, its target is closer to the expert rating than to the average of their ratings.
chart.introSelect: Select a bar, or a study in the table below, to read the study and the expert's feedback.
chart.canvasLabel: Bar chart of the participants' mean rating for each study, with 95% confidence intervals and the expert rating. The table below gives the same figures.
chart.tooltipMeanSingle: Participant mean: {mean} (n = 1, too few for an interval)
chart.tooltipFooter: Click or tap to read the study
chart.summary: {rated} of {total} studies have participant ratings. For {close} of them, the participant mean is within one point of the expert rating.
chart.summaryNone: No study has participant ratings yet.
chart.failed: The chart could not be loaded. The table below has the same figures.

table.heading: Statistics by study
table.intro: Every figure comes from participant ratings only; the expert's rating has its own column. 'Ratings' is the number of participants who rated the study, 'SD' (standard deviation) shows how much their ratings vary and '95% CI' is the confidence interval for the mean. 'Mean prediction' is the average of participants' predictions of the crowd's rating for the study. A dash means there are too few ratings: the SD and the interval need at least two.
table.sortHint: Select a column heading to sort the table. The 95% CI column sorts by its lower limit.
table.regionLabel: Statistics by study (scrolls sideways on small screens)

target.other: The game would score a new prediction for this study against a target of {target}: the expert rating counted as {weight} participants, combined with all {count} participant ratings so far (from every room).
